The examples below are ordered from simplest to most advanced. Each one introduces new features on top of the previous examples.

## Minimal calendar

The simplest possible calendar. Events are defined directly in the YAML front matter under a named key (here `minimal`), and then rendered with the `toastui` shortcode referencing that key. The default view is week view.

Every event needs at least three fields: `title`, `start`, and `end`. date time must be specified in this format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`. The calendar defaults to **today's date** rather than the event date. And this would look like a blank calendar even though the event is present in the calendar. Therefore, it is recommended to always provide a `date` field.

```yaml
---
toastui:
  minimal:
    date: "2026-04-01"
    events:
      - title: "Big event"
        start: "2026-04-01T10:00:00"
        end: "2026-04-01T16:00:00"
---
```

```markdown
{{{< toastui minimal >}}}
```

{{< toastui minimal >}}

## Month view

The user can change to different views such as **month**, **day**, or **week** views, but you can initially set the default view using the `defaultView` field in the calendar configuration. Here is a single event in **month** view. The user can be disallowed from changing the view if `navigation` is set to `false`.

```yaml
---
toastui:
  month-view:
    defaultView: month
    date: "2026-04-01"
    events:
      - title: "Big event"
        start: "2026-04-01T10:00:00"
        end: "2026-04-01T16:00:00"
---
```

```markdown
{{{< toastui month-view >}}}
```

{{< toastui month-view >}}

## Day view

Switch to a **day** view to see a detailed hour-by-hour timeline. This is useful when you want to focus on a single day's agenda. Set `defaultView: day` and set `date` to the target day.

```yaml
toastui:
  day-view:
    defaultView: day
    date: "2026-04-15"
    events:
      - title: "Standup"
        start: "2026-04-15T09:00:00"
        end: "2026-04-15T09:30:00"
      - title: "Deep Work"
        start: "2026-04-15T10:00:00"
        end: "2026-04-15T12:00:00"
      - title: "Lunch"
        start: "2026-04-15T12:00:00"
        end: "2026-04-15T13:00:00"
      - title: "Code Review"
        start: "2026-04-15T14:00:00"
        end: "2026-04-15T15:30:00"
```

```markdown
{{{< toastui day-view >}}}
```

{{< toastui day-view >}}

## Categories and Duration

In week and day views, we can see different categories of events, namely **Milestone**, **Task** and **All Day** events. This is defined using the `category` field in the event data. We have updated the YAML metadata to include different event categories. We can also limit the displayed daily durations for each day by specifying `hourStart` and `hourEnd`.

```yaml
toastui:
  categories-and-duration:
    defaultView: day
    date: "2026-04-15"
    week:
      hourStart: 9
      hourEnd: 17
    events:
      - title: "Standup"
        category: time
        start: "2026-04-15T09:00:00"
        end: "2026-04-15T09:30:00"
      - title: "Deep Work"
        category: task
        start: "2026-04-15T10:00:00"
        end: "2026-04-15T12:00:00"
      - title: "Lunch"
        start: "2026-04-15T12:00:00"
        end: "2026-04-15T13:00:00"
      - title: "Code Review"
        category: "milestone"
        start: "2026-04-15T14:00:00"
        end: "2026-04-15T15:30:00"
      - title: "Picnic"
        category: "allday"
        start: "2026-04-16"
        end: "2026-04-16"
        isAllday: true
```

```markdown
{{{< toastui categories-and-duration >}}}
```

{{< toastui categories-and-duration >}}

The display of categories **Task** and **Milestone** can be controlled using `taskView` by setting it as `true`, `false`, `milestone` or `task`.

```yaml
toastui:
  categories-and-duration:
    week:
      taskView: false
```

```yaml
toastui:
  categories-and-duration:
    week:
      taskView: 'milestone'
```

## All-day and multi-day events

Events can span entire days or stretch across multiple days. Set `category: allday` and `isAllday: true` for all-day events. They are rendered in a banner at the top of the calendar. Regular timed events appear alongside them in the time grid.

```yaml
events:
  - title: "Sprint Planning"
    category: allday
    start: "2026-04-14"
    end: "2026-04-14"
    isAllday: true
  - title: "Conference"
    category: allday
    start: "2026-04-16"
    end: "2026-04-18"
    isAllday: true
    backgroundColor: "#ff6b6b"
  - title: "Workshop"
    category: time
    start: "2026-04-15T09:00:00"
    end: "2026-04-15T12:00:00"
```

```markdown
{{{< toastui allday >}}}
```

{{< toastui allday >}}

## Calendars

This example introduces **calendars** — named colour groups that let you visually distinguish event categories. Each event references a calendar via `calendarId`.

```yaml
toastui:
  calendars:
    defaultView: week
    date: "2026-04-09"
    events:
      - title: "Morning Run"
        calendarId: cal1
        category: time
        start: "2026-04-09T06:00:00"
        end: "2026-04-09T07:00:00"
      - title: "Team Standup"
        calendarId: cal2
        category: time
        start: "2026-04-09T09:00:00"
        end: "2026-04-09T09:30:00"
      - title: "Design Review"
        calendarId: cal2
        category: time
        start: "2026-04-10T14:00:00"
        end: "2026-04-10T15:30:00"
    calendars:
      - id: cal1
        name: Personal
        backgroundColor: "#03bd9e"
      - id: cal2
        name: Work
        backgroundColor: "#00a9ff"
```

```markdown
{{{< toastui calendars >}}}
```

{{< toastui calendars >}}

## Event and popup details

Use `eventDetailItems` to add optional details inside timed events. Enable `useDetailPopup: true` and use `popupDetailItems` to select optional popup rows independently. Both accept any field in the event data, including custom columns from delimited files. Known TOAST UI fields such as `location` and `attendees` use their native icons; custom fields render as `field: value`. Both options default to no optional details and only show selected fields that exist in the event data. Popup title and date are always visible. Set `timeFormat` to `"12h"` or `"24h"` to use one format for rendered timed event labels, the time-grid axis, the current-time indicator, and this popup. The default is `"24h"`. The separate event form popup time picker remains in TOAST UI's built-in 24-hour format.

```yaml
toastui:

  popup:
    defaultView: week
    date: "2026-04-14"
    useDetailPopup: true
    eventDetailItems:
      - location
      - attendees
      - project
    popupDetailItems:
      - location
      - attendees
      - project
    timeFormat: "24h"
    calendars:
      - id: cal1
        name: Work
        color: "#ffffff"
        backgroundColor: "#00a9ff"
        dragBackgroundColor: "#00a9ff"
        borderColor: "#00a9ff"
    events:
      - title: "Design Review"
        calendarId: cal1
        category: time
        start: "2026-04-14T09:00:00"
        end: "2026-04-14T11:30:00"
        location: "Room A"
        attendees: "Alice"
        project: "Apollo"
      - title: "Sprint Retro"
        calendarId: cal1
        category: time
        start: "2026-04-15T14:00:00"
        end: "2026-04-15T15:00:00"
        location: "Main Hall"
        attendees: "Bob"
        project: "Gemini"
```

```markdown
{{{< toastui popup >}}}
```

{{< toastui popup >}}

## Events from a TSV file

Instead of listing events in YAML, point `file` to a **tab-separated** file and set `file-sep` to `"\t"`. Here is the format of the TSV file:

```tsv
id	calendarId	title	category	start	end	isAllday	location	backgroundColor
101	cal1	TSV Demo Meeting	time	2026-04-14T09:00:00	2026-04-14T10:00:00	false	Room North	#03bd9e
102	cal2	TSV Sprint Review	time	2026-04-15T13:00:00	2026-04-15T14:00:00	false	Studio B	#00a9ff
103	cal1	TSV Planning Day	allday	2026-04-16	2026-04-16	true	HQ	#03bd9e
```

The file must have a header row with at least the columns `title`, `start`, and `end`. Optional columns like `calendarId`, `category`, `location`, and `backgroundColor` are picked up automatically.

```yaml
toastui:
  tsv-events:
    defaultView: month
    date: "2026-04-01"
    height: 620px
    file: data/events.tsv
    file-sep: "\t"
```

```markdown
{{{< toastui tsv-events >}}}
```

{{< toastui tsv-events >}}

## Events from a CSV file

Comma-delimited files work the same way — just change `file-sep` to `","`. Here is a preview of the CSV file format:

```csv
id,calendarId,title,category,start,end,isAllday,location,backgroundColor
201,cal1,CSV Demo Meeting,time,2026-04-17T09:30:00,2026-04-17T10:15:00,false,Room East,#03bd9e
202,cal2,CSV Design Sync,time,2026-04-18T14:00:00,2026-04-18T15:00:00,false,Online,#00a9ff
203,cal2,CSV Release Day,allday,2026-04-19,2026-04-19,true,Remote,#00a9ff
```

This example also uses the **week** view so you can see the timed events on the grid.

```yaml
toastui:
  csv-events:
    defaultView: week
    date: "2026-04-17"
    file: data/events.csv
    file-sep: ","
```

```markdown
{{{< toastui csv-events >}}}
```

{{< toastui csv-events >}}

## Fully inline shortcode

You can skip YAML metadata entirely and pass **all** options directly in the shortcode. This style is handy for quick one-off calendars or prototypes. Note that inline arguments cannot express complex nested structures like `calendars` or `week` options.

```markdown
{{{< toastui file="data/events.tsv" file-sep="\t" defaultView="day" date="2026-04-15" >}}}
```

{{< toastui file="data/events.tsv" file-sep="\t" defaultView="day" date="2026-04-15" >}}

## Inline override of metadata

You can **combine** YAML metadata with inline arguments. The metadata key provides the base configuration, and any inline arguments override individual values. Here the `week-view` config is reused but switched to month view with a different date and height.

```markdown
{{{< toastui week-view defaultView="month" date="2026-04-01" height="500px" >}}}
```

{{< toastui week-view defaultView="month" date="2026-04-01" height="500px" >}}

## Full-featured schedule

This example puts it all together: events loaded from a CSV file, custom calendar colours for different event types, detail popups, timezone configuration, a workweek-only week view with custom hour range, and an enlarged time grid. This pattern is well suited for multi-day workshops and conference programmes. `height` and `timegridHeight` are manually set to remove scroll bar.

```yaml
toastui:
  schedule:
    defaultView: week
    file: "data/schedule.csv"
    file-sep: ","
    date: "2026-11-16"
    useDetailPopup: true
    height: 960px
    timegridHeight: 900px
    week:
      workweek: true
      taskView: false
      eventView: ['time']
      hourStart: 9
      hourEnd: 21
      showNowIndicator: true
    timezone:
      zones:
        - timezoneName: Europe/Stockholm
    eventDetailItems:
      - attendees
    popupDetailItems:
      - attendees
      - calendar
    calendars:
      - id: "session"
        name: "Session"
        backgroundColor: "#D6EAF8"
        borderColor: "#85C1E9"
      - id: "free"
        name: "Free"
        backgroundColor: "#FCF3CF"
        borderColor: "#F7DC6F"
      - id: "extra"
        name: "Extra"
        backgroundColor: "#E8DAEF"
        borderColor: "#BB8FCE"
```

```markdown
{{{< toastui schedule >}}}
```

{{< toastui schedule >}}

## Limitations

- RevealJS is supported but known to be flaky
- For other formats, the shortcode emits no output
- Short duration events may not be displayed legibly depending on the max day duration
- The calendar may not display legibly on very small screens

```yaml
---
toastui:
  limitations:
    date: "2026-04-01"
    events:
    - title: "30 min event"
      start: "2026-04-01T10:00:00"
      end: "2026-04-01T10:30:00"
    - title: "15 min event"
      start: "2026-04-01T11:00:00"
      end: "2026-04-01T11:15:00"
    - title: "10 min event"
      start: "2026-04-01T12:00:00"
      end: "2026-04-01T12:10:00"
    - title: "5 min event"
      start: "2026-04-01T13:00:00"
      end: "2026-04-01T13:05:00"
---
```

```markdown
{{{< toastui limitations >}}}
```
